title: 18.5 A Rail-to-Rail 3rd-Order Noise-Shaping SAR ADC Achieving 105.4dB SFDR with Integrated Input Buffer Using Continuous-Time Correlated Level Shifting
problem: High-resolution SAR ADCs (>13b) require large capacitive DACs to meet kT/C noise specs, heavily loading the input buffer. Buffer driving large CDAC while achieving rail-to-rail swing and linearity dominates power consumption, becoming the efficiency bottleneck.
motivation: Energy-efficient ADC design is bottlenecked by input buffer power as resolution increases; integrating buffer functionality into the SAR loop can reduce overall system power consumption.
method: A SAR analog-to-digital converter that uses the full available voltage range incorporates continuous-time correlated level shifting (continuously adjusting its reference level in real-time) in the input buffer to maintain signal accuracy while driving large capacitor arrays. This level-shifting technique is built directly into the noise-shaping feedback loop (which shifts unwanted electronic noise to frequencies that don't affect accuracy). By combining these techniques, the design avoids needing a higher power supply voltage.
key_novelty: Continuous-time correlated level shifting (adjusting the reference level in real-time) enables the input buffer to integrate directly into the SAR noise-shaping loop while maintaining rail-to-rail voltage swing and avoiding higher power supply requirements.
contributions: Rail-to-rail 3rd-order noise-shaping SAR ADC achieving 105.4dB SFDR
Integrated input buffer reducing driving pressure on capacitive DAC
Continuous-time level shifting maintaining linearity at reduced cost
primary_theme: integrated input buffer SAR ADC with noise-shaping
